#4306. Grammy Award-Winning Composer Austin Wintory Shares His Early Musical Drafts Intended For Mass Effect 5

Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

#4304. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4303. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

#4302. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Goes Free for a Limited Time

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

Call of Duty will always be a major force in the gaming zeitgeist; that much is certain, but the recent success of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was a much-needed win for the franchise. With the campaign receiving fantastic reception, the multiplayer rolling out, and the inclusion of the extraction mode DMZ, Activision is looking to keep racking up wins.

Former Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith says Todd Howard knows when to make things simpler for players, and recalls a design decision that proved him wrong.

Their newest incentive was announced on the official Call of Duty Twitter: Modern Warfare 4’s DMZ is free to play for all until November 11th, giving new and returning players a taste of extraction action exclusive to the Modern Warfare reboot series. Serving as MW’s answer to Zombies, the mode has been totally revamped in preparation for new blood.

DMZ has stuck with the Modern Warfare reboot series since MW2, serving as the title’s unique mode alongside Black Ops Zombies. While Zombies leaned into the absurd paranoia and conspiracies that swirl around undercover operations, DMZ focuses on the realism and boots-on-the-ground feel that originally made Warzone work so well, playing off Modern Warfare’s thematic strengths.

MW4’s DMZ dropped only a few days ago, but has already hit the ground running, with story missions, PvE encounters, and plenty of incentives to play cool or callous when other players show. Packed with new weapons, gear, and locations, MW4’s DMZ is set on the Korean Peninsula, Hajin, where the devastation that rocked the campaign is still felt.

Stuck between squadrons of NPC soldiers, a dangerous map, and the X factor of players, the free trial will populate Hajin even more, sparking hijinks and carefully curated tactics in equal measure. Any progress made by players during their free playtime will translate to progression in the main game, giving prospective players a hit of the game’s action without asking for the full $69.99.

With the campaign receiving fantastic reception, the multiplayer rolling out, and the inclusion of the extraction mode DMZ, Activision is looking to keep racking up wins.

That price tag is honestly the biggest pain point for many players, but Modern Warfare 4’s new rewards for completing weapon progression, multiple modes with a variety of unlocks, and a phenomenal upgrade of the franchise’s gunplay make it a solid buy for anyone content with sticking to a single title for a while.

MW4’s reinventions were fully needed to pull the subseries out of the total rut that was Modern Warfare 3, and it’s incredibly exciting to see where the game will go both with its internal modes and as a guiding star for the franchise going forward. Black Ops might be up next on the rotation, but there’s no shame in taking notes from your neighbor.

Call of Duty stands alongside Grand Theft Auto as major gaming icons that have avoided aligning with any specific platform. While GTA 6 is releasing on PC at a later date, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 dropped everywhere simultaneously, even on the Switch 2. The title’s sales give universal releases a good argument, even as console first-party titles are being tied back down.

With the gaming community finally back on its side, Modern Warfare 4 has some big opportunities to recover the franchise’s PR, which has been stumbling after questionable cosmetics and stuttering quality. Modern Warfare 4 is sticking to its aesthetic and goals well for now, but time will only tell if Warzone’s inclusion will make odd collabs start slinking in.

Infinity Ward has some time to rest on their laurels and focus on live service updates, with Season 1’s launch already bringing players back in. With a full DMZ trial, a good chunk of players are sure to stick around, even if those already in the game treat them like easy pickings for the duration.

As GTA 6's launch approaches, everyone wants part of the PR pie, including internet ISPs.

#4301. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4297. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4295. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4294. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4292. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4291. Cozy Magical Sim Witchbrook Gets A January Release Date

Witchbrook is a game I've been looking forward to for a while, and today's Nintendo Indie World showcase finally confirmed the game's release date: January 28. Any game from Chucklefish, best known for publishing Stardew Valley and developing the Wargroove series, is worthy of my attention, and Witchbrook looks more exciting the more we see of it. See it for yourself in the release date trailer below.

The game mixes cute pixel art with a robust suite of magical gameplay systems. As you go to a witch college to learn spells, you'll also build a life in the town, making friends, working jobs, decorating your home, and more. It was an appealing pitch when it was announced nearly 10 years ago in 2017, and it remains so to this day. After a long stretch of relative silence, last year the game was scheduled to launch sometime in 2026. Obviously, the team has faced some delays since then, but we're just glad it's actually coming out.

Witchbrook's release date was announced during today's Nintendo-specific stream, but it's coming to all major platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC.

A Snail’s Tale (Something Classic, 11th Nov, $12.99) - A retro RPG that asks the age old question: would you take a world of riches in exchange for being chased by an immortal, killer snail? Once upon a time, a commoner was granted his wish to become the king of a vast nation. In exchange, he is constantly chased by an immortal killer snail. Now the king is facing his end of the bargain.

Arcade Archives PREHISTORIC ISLE (HAMSTER, 29th Oct, $7.99) - "PREHISTORIC ISLE" is a shooting game released by SNK in 1989. As the protagonist heads to Greenhell Island to investigate a series of shipwrecks off the coast of the Bahamas, prehistoric dragons thought to have gone extinct launch a relentless attack. The option unit equipped to your aircraft can be repositioned to change its attack method into 5 different types based on its location, such as firing flame lasers upward or dropping bombs diagonally downward. Make full use of your option unit to face various obstacles and uncover the truth behind the mysterious shipwrecks!

Big Jhow Jet (Nerd Games, 7th Nov, $6.99) - Prepare for takeoff! Strap on your homemade jetpack, defy gravity, and unleash total chaos to save your friends from the dreaded Bacon Factory! Jhow is a brilliant, tech-obsessed piglet whose peaceful farm life is shattered when an ominous corporate truck kidnaps all his friends.

Black Lily’s Tale (1000-REKA, 29th Oct, $13.00) - Includes a Nintendo Switch™-exclusive After Story & all DLC scenarios! ―――What is Black Lily's Tale? "Black Lily's Tale", featuring delicate and beautiful art by Fukahire. A unique choice-making systems that will have you seeing visual novel decisions in a whole new light. Pure but not naive, classic but not cliché. A yuri game that will make you strive toward the best ending! You can intervene and lead these girls to happiness.

Castlebound (Ogre Pixel, 11th Nov, $9.99) - Fight hordes of evil monsters and defend your castle in this 1-4 player action platformer with Roguelike elements! Cat-Astrophy (Pdpartid@games, 5th Nov, $14.99) - Cat-Astrophy is a fast-paced, challenging space action roguelite: its Star Cursor system and evolving modules force you to adapt your build and playstyle in every run, generating chaotic combat and precise jumps. Don Bradman Cricket JR (Tru Blu Games, 5th Nov, $19.99) - Out of the highly successful Don Bradman simulation series comes Don Bradman JR, the hard-hitting arcade cricket game. Faraway (Annapurna Interactive, 5th Nov, $7.99) - Faraway is an endless procedurally generated, mastery-driven arcade game about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive. Gemporium (Merge Conflict Studio, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Grow your small gem business in this short, casual simulation miner, Gemporium! Hillthorn (Raw Fury, 10th Nov, $14.99) - Only the foolish and the desperate attempt to wander the mazelike trails of Hillthorn. But a child has gone missing, time is in short supply, and you’re the one being tasked with unraveling the mountain’s secrets. Welcome to Hillthorn, a dark investigation game unlike any other, where the mystery unfolds without a single word spoken.

HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition (Electric Airship, 31st Oct, $17.99) - Your next-door neighbors are zombies, reanimated monsters deliver the mail and ghosts hide out in your bathroom. Next of Kin: Epiphany (Spelkvall, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Step into the world of "Next of Kin: Epiphany," where you become private detective Dennis Monroe, a relentless investigator driven to catch the infamous "Epiphany Killer," a shadowy figure who has haunted the city for over twenty years. Nyghtmare: The Ninth King (Caracal Games, 31st Oct, $4.99) - Centuries after vanishing without a trace, the Kingdom of Mortemire suddenly reappears. Armed with only an iron whip, she ventures into its decaying streets in search of answers, facing the creatures and dangers that have taken hold of the land. #4288. Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year update brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire update’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

You’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. #4287. 10 Most Extravagant Video Games of 2026

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

As someone who's been playing and analyzing games for practically half my life, I've been getting increasingly hard to impress within the interactive entertainment industry after having experienced all sorts of things.

However, this insensitivity to the regular attempts to offer a unique campaign isn't impenetrable, as every year there are developers who manage to break through my shell of apathy and leave a truly strong impression.

Whether they're good or bad games—since the ability to surprise isn't always linked to quality—I always enjoy a campaign that evokes new sensations, given it's become increasingly rare.

Therefore, if you're looking for the kind of adventure that generates feelings you can't even describe, I recommend you try any of these ten most extravagant video games of 2026.

Games that follow in Pokémon's footsteps have left me indifferent for a very long time, but I didn't expect that one of the titles that would hook me the most this year would be Grombo Card Shop Tycoon, the early access version of a game that emulates buying and selling booster packs from the famous franchise.

With simply phenomenal humor and magnificent creature design, brimming with pop culture references, this title strikes a tremendously satisfying balance between incremental mechanics and shop management, becoming exhilarating very quickly.

Dealing with customers looking for specific cards and others who want to bet on whether they'll sell you one for double the price or give it to you for free, deciding what to sell and at what price, decorating to your liking, filling the enormous skill tree... It's a satire that's as conscious and funny as it is addictive.

Never in a million years would I have imagined that opening dozens of booster packs from my own business to find golden feces with a face or a Charizard made of sausage would be so satisfying, but Grombo Card Shop Tycoon made it a reality.

Remember the LCD aesthetic of the Game & Watch? Me neither, until I stumbled across Future Knight by accident and fell completely in love with its take on a rather forgotten variant of retro gaming.

Based solely on its glorious and unique visual style, the title's presence on this list is practically essential, but if we add the plot, a homunculus tumor inside a robot who travels to the past to defeat the tyranny of a cultist who erased humanity's memory and set up a pyramid scheme as a cult, it becomes even more compelling.

Regardless, the gameplay is equally impressive, as you control both the android, based on a 90s soap opera protagonist, and the tiny companion, resulting in an extremely fun 2D action-platformer with challenging bosses and spectacular animations.

Given its arcade-style focus, Future Knight lasts three hours yet will win you over for life, especially since, unless you're approaching old age, I'm sure you've never played anything remotely similar.

Ever since I played Ghostrunner at launch, I've been forever linked to One More Level and everything bearing its name, though even with that affection, I couldn't have imagined what Valor Mortis would bring.

The Soulslike genre is usually quite traditional and rigidly adheres to its conventions, but the studio decided to focus more on its own expertise than on FromSoftware's legacy, resulting in the only game of its kind where movement is a delight.

William inherits Jack's motion abilities in a first-person action title that's an ARPG, an FPS, and a parkour experience simultaneously, blending all sorts of gameplay concepts and philosophies that one wouldn't think should work together, yet they do so magnificently.

Add to that magnificent worldbuilding in an apocalyptic France of Napoleon Bonaparte, some of the best level design the genre has ever seen, and particularly high production values compared to its peers, and Valor Mortis becomes a rather particular specimen.

If you want to spend the autumn in the safest yet most violent way, I invite you to play the ten best action games that you need to play in fall 2026.

Faith: The Unholy Trinity is among the best horror video games I've ever played, and Tenebris Somnia became the finest spiritual successor I could have imagined for such an outstanding production.

Instead of rotoscoping, the game uses cinematic cutscenes with live actors and real sets, complemented by spectacular makeup and editing work that blends seamlessly with the title's refined pixel art to create otherworldly, bizarre, and terrifying creatures.

From its themes and levels to its creative puzzles and fascinating story and mythology, Tenebris Somnia is one of the most distinctive references the genre has seen in the entire decade, as easy to spot among hundreds of titles as finding an anvil in a haystack.

Because of its fundamental ideas and the perfect pacing with which it moves between video game and cinematic experience, you'll never expect the kind of story that awaits you, much less the fidelity with which that story is translated into gameplay.

Inside the AAA spectrum, few developers are as functionally eccentric as Capcom, which, as Pragmata demonstrates, doesn't need to sacrifice experimentation to deliver a truly enjoyable title.

The campaign unfolds through the dichotomies of hacking and shooting, Hugh's brutishness and Diana's innocence, the slow pace and dynamic levels, and so on with every element that constitutes it, because it doesn't run away from the tension of conflicting concepts.

It's an emotional and charismatic story, set against its backdrop so that, along with the spirited gameplay, it never stops moving forward, always feeling like a fresh and captivating experience that you never want to stop playing.

Most big-budget products avoid contradictions and risks, and therein lies Pragmata's extravagance: going against the grain of its class and prioritizing its creative vision above all else.

Kyle Thompson's craftsmanship is becoming increasingly refined with each new Metroidvania he releases, but he has truly outdone himself in every conceivable way with Well Dweller.

Speaking of contrasts, his latest adventure leaves you feeling both profoundly unsettled and captivated by its environments and inhabitants, as the juxtaposition of gorgeous biomes and atmospheric music with gothic and unsettling designs is mesmerizing.

Fighting bosses whose behaviors and aesthetics seem lifted from sleep paralysis is magnificent, even when it involves giant hands chasing you through the pipes of a kingdom, a dollmaker trapping your sister's soul in a plush toy, or a guardian decapitated by the moon to possess his body.

Well Dweller is a collection of fables and legends seen through the lens of its action-adventure gameplay, which, needless to say, is extraordinary and offers some of the best structures in the entire genre in terms of combat, movement, exploration, and progression.

The strategy genre displays extraordinary depth, and offers some truly unique and underrated titles.

"Extravagant" means unusual, striking, and peculiar, so I can't think of better adjectives to describe Phantom Blade Zero, which continues Black Myth: Wukong's work in breaking down cultural barriers related to China.

The video game industry of this Asian giant had only previously showcased its talent on a large scale in the mobile ecosystem, but projects like S-Game's open our minds to the world of possibilities that comes with seeing the interactive medium through their eyes.

The result? A glorious action game that can't be reduced to being inspired by one or another benchmark of the genre, but rather driven by Chinese idiosyncrasies in terms of functionality, visual identity, narrative, mechanics, and sound, offering a unique journey both on paper and in execution.

Among everything released this year, Phantom Blade Zero is by far one of the most exciting and culturally significant products, something we can't say about half of the creations that boast its production values.

If Remedy Entertainment ever releases a video game that isn't an enlightening, mind-blowing experience, I'll be the first to speak out, but Control Resonant shows us that we'll still have to wait to see if that day ever comes.

The sheer audacity of making such drastic changes from its predecessor, especially after Alan Wake 2's financial hardships, is the kind of gallantry we must praise, support, and cherish to keep the art of video games alive, because it transcends mere commercial success.

Consequently, we got a title whose story, setting, characters, enemies, and even gameplay systems transcend the ordinary, becoming part of those special titles you can only sum up as "I can't tell you about it; you have to experience it".

Even though Control Resonant isn't among my top titles from the studio, it's still magnificent and light-years ahead of what the average developer can achieve, proving once again that Remedy simply operates in a league of its own.

If you’re looking for fast-paced titles to violently lose yourself in, here are ten action games most people haven’t played but definitely should.

The name Edmund McMillen has become synonymous with irreverence, weirdness, and iconic status, as you can see games like Mewgenics from miles away and still have every fiber of your being know who created it and what to expect.

However, even with full awareness of its creator's unsettling talent, mere mortals aren't prepared to anticipate the absurd display of depth, inventiveness, and ability to cohere oddities into one of the most addictive products in video game history.

I don't know what it says about our industry that such adjectives can be applied to a work that consists of breeding cats with autism, ADHD, cancer, bipolar disorder, and other conditions to battle in turn-based duels against "fetus-like enemies", feces, or angel pigeons, but I'm glad nonetheless.

If you have the willpower to dedicate less than hundreds of hours to Mewgenics, I applaud you, but I'm not that strong, because I'm afraid I have a weakness for roguelites that have more quirkiness than pixels.

Now, the 2026 game that most often left me speechless, simply because I couldn't believe what I was seeing, is Romeo is a Dead Man, which is completely to be expected if you know who Suda51 is.

Author-driven video games aren't as common a phenomenon as they are in film, but Goichi Suda is an exception to the rule precisely because of how he can take a story so often repeated throughout the centuries across every imaginable artistic medium and still make it original.

You think you know the Romeo and Juliet fable, though Romeo is a Dead Man thoroughly subverts it to create a title with mechanics from hack and slash, visual novel, on-rails shooter, third-person shooter, creature management, and other genres I can't even name.

An intergalactic, interdimensional, and intertemporal twisted love story that plays with the rules of the universe as much as with our expectations couldn't help but be extravagant, yet that's just how the great Suda51 works.

I'd venture to say it's far from being the best game on the list, but that hardly matters because, when it comes to being unique, everyone would have to ask for its blessing just to even enter the conversation.

From the distant ICO to the recent Desktop Explorer, these are ten adventure games you can finish in under 10 hours.

#4286. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4280. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4279. 10 Sega Genesis JRPGs Most Haven’t Played, But Definitely Should

Zackari Greif is a List Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2021. A lifelong gamer and former writer for GameRant and Fix Gaming Channel, Zackari has written across news, guides, interviews, previews, reviews, features, and lists, bringing a broad background in gaming journalism to h

When you think of the JRPG subgenre, you think of PlayStation or the SNES. I can’t refute that Sony and Nintendo earned their stake in that video game niche as a big Kingdom Hearts and Final Fantasy 7 fan. But there’s one other console that had an expansive library of titles in that area.

Even though it was most known for its war against Nintendo and the start of Sonic the Hedgehog’s 35-year-long running streak, the Sega Genesis had a number of good JRPGs on it over the years. Games like Phantasy Star and Landstalker have been widely noticed, but most of them are only recognized by die-hard Sega fans.

Sega's 16-bit console era has left its mark on the video game industry in ways we still see today.

As a big Sega fan myself, (to a point,) I’m here to help navigate you through some Sega JRPGs you’ve most likely left behind or just weren’t around to experience. Don’t worry, we’ve got plenty to dig into.

Back in the day, and even now, Crusader of Centy has been seen as Sega’s The Legend of Zelda clone. In truth, it has a few elements that help separate it from Link’s adventures, but the biggest is that it was actually made as part of a big Genesis-based RPG push in Japan. We’ll be talking about more of these games as we go.

Out of all the games released through this initiative, I feel like Crusader of Centy is the most well-known. But out of the people who know about it, there’s a stark divide. Retro JRPG fans have likely played it, but how many Sega fans outside of that have actually experienced it? The only thing you might know about it is the fact that Sonic’s in it. Yeah. I said it.

I believe it’s a game really worth playing. It harkens back to an era where RPG and adventure game mechanics weren’t so strictly divided. Crusader of Centy also focuses pretty heavily on exploration and discovery, namely in the way that animal companions give you abilities you only get through mixing them up. There’s a lot here for almost everyone.

I know, I know, calling Beyond Oasis a JRPG is a little controversial. Its top-down, open combat and varying challenges make it hard to call it much of anything. That’s the trouble with these games sometimes. Genres were hardly the big defining points of a game as they are now, and a lot of games got to experiment with what they offered.

In the case of Beyond Oasis, if it has story beats like an RPG, has magic you can level up like an RPG no matter how basic, and has rewards for exploring through the map like an RPG, then it’s an RPG. Even if you disagree, I’m sure you agree that more people need to play this game. It’s one of the few Sega Genesis games that play this way, and it’s gorgeous to look at on top of it. If you haven’t played Beyond Oasis, I highly recommend it.

You’ve likely heard of the Shining Force series if you’re familiar with retro JRPGs. It’s one of the most highly regarded options for the genre that the Sega Genesis had, coming second to Phantasy Star itself. The first two games are on Nintendo Switch Online’s Classic offerings, even. But because of a number of different factors, like its name or its formula changes, Shining in the Darkness isn’t mentioned a lot because it hasn’t been played a lot.

For those not in the know, many of the Shining Force games are tactical RPGs. Shining in the Darkness is the first game in the series, and it was a dungeon crawler instead. It’s a very classic dungeon crawler, too, resembling a strange combination between Dragon Quest’s presentation and Wizardry’s systems.

It very much feels like a Shining game through and through, thankfully. It’s spectacularly paced like the later games are, which makes it a great introduction to the genre. It’s also less of a pain than some of it’s contemporaries at the time. We’ve all had that struggle where a retro game is a bit tougher than we expected, right? You won’t run into that here.

For every Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics that have managed to beat the odds and become popular and prominent tactical JRPGs, there’s about ten other games that didn’t get as big of a chance to shine. To me, Warrior of Rome is one of them. It leans a bit more close to something like Civilization but it I feel like I’m just playing a Fire Emblem competitor above anything else.

And it’s very fun! The first time I discovered this game, I kind of sat there and played it for three hours, completely transfixed. It’s a fairly rudimentary game, but ordering my soldiers and watching them all fight was still entertaining, even if the graphics weren’t the best the Genesis could do. Besides, Warrior of Rome tracked multiple battles I had across the map in real-time, and that was really impressive to see on the Genesis of all things. I feel like more tactical JRPG fans could try this game out. It’s a nice little snack while you wait for the bigger pillars in this little niche.

We’re back at another Zelda-like action RPG of the old days! Togi O: King Colossus is one of those games that just gets you right into what you want. You’re given simple exposition, you get a mission from the old man you live with, and get out there. If only the game was that easy on its players.

Togi O is a game with a lot of fighting. For some of you, that’s great. For others, it’ll be the most annoying thing you’ve ever dealt with on the Sega Genesis. Enemies are allowed to deal whatever punches they can throw at you, while nine times out of ten, you’re going to be left with a low-range weapon to use. It’s not exactly fair.

You also need to defeat all these enemies In crowded dungeon rooms to get items you need to progress. Items that are part of one big fetch quest, mind you. Argh. But even with all of this, Togi O might be the last stone left unturned for some of you die-hard fans out there. And like Crusader of Centy, it’s a good, retro relic that could use more eyes on it. Give it a try if you want a bit of a nostalgic challenge.

There are many elements and mechanics that JRPGs borrowed from other genres to create their wonderful works.

Back in 1991, Sega entered a strange, fleeting partnership with what’s one of the more obscure yet important JRPG developers out there, Nihon Falcom. This partnership would only last around four years, but it would lead to some important ports of Falcom games under and joint name “Sega Falcom.” One of these would be Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes.

Now, Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes was on a number of consoles, including the SNES, but the Genesis version in particular has impressively better visuals. Plus, if you’re here, you’ll likely prefer the Genesis sound font anyway.

Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes on Genesis does away with the big, bordered display with all of the menus around it and gives you the entire screen to work with. This allows sprites to breathe and big moments and battles to shine more because of it. Even if you’ve played Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes some other way, like maybe with its PSP portable remake, I still think this version is worth experiencing. It really shines on the Genesis. And that might be through the partnership that helped it thrive.

Now this is where things get interesting. There are a lot of great JRPGs on the Sega Genesis that everyone has likely played, but even at the bottom of the barrel, there’s some hidden gems. Braver Battle Saga: Legend of the Magic Warrior is one of those games. It’s an unlicensed Sega Genesis game that dates back as far as 1996. It’s earned notoriety for being a pretty good game despite lacking the golden Sega seal of approval on the box.

It’s a classic JRPG through and through despite that. Complete with quaint little towns, a rip-off ATB system, and battle music that will make you hate how many encounters there are in this game. Great for players who think the JRPGs of the olden days are better than what we’re getting now. Because of how great this game feels and plays, it’s been restored officially with modern releases and an English translation that you can find on Steam. If you’ve been craving a retro hidden gem to come out of nowhere like this, then this game is exactly what you’re looking for.

If you loved Final Fantasy Resonance, then it's time for more JRPG love, Jobs, and pixel art.

If you’ve been digging through Sega Genesis games, looking for all the RPGs that the system has to offer, then you might have heard of this one before. I tend to harp on this one a lot because it’s a baffling and head-spinning obscure game that I feel like those self-proclaimed experts of the genre should check out. Maten no Soumetsu is well-known for being impressive visually and incredibly punishing with its difficulty.

If you feel incredibly powerful because you beat Elden Ring, or just want to suffer with a game that’s truly unforgivingly hard, I dare you to pick up this one and report back to me. Good luck!

If you’re here, I’m assuming you really like mechas. Or anime. Or Fire Emblem. Happen to be a fan the first and third ones? Boy, do I have the game for you! Vixen 357 is a war strategy JRPG that brings mechas and the same staples of Fire Emblem to one fantastic Sega Genesis game.

As you might expect, you control units in the form of human-piloted mechs. I state this kind of obvious fact because Vixen 357 pulls no punches, and it shows you the pilots bleeding before the permadeath mechanics take them away. This, combined with some gorgeous graphics, is why Vixen 357 has been saved and has recently been ported to modern consoles through Ratalaika Games and Shinyuden. Go check it out!

Remember when I spoke about an initiative back in the day that aimed to put more JRPGs on the Sega Genesis in Japan? Some games made its way over, but not all of them. Surging Aura is one of those games. It’s circled around the import and translation scene for years as a great game that was locked behind the lack of a full translation.

I’m happy to report that in the time since I last wrote about Surging Aura, a full English translation patch has been completed! Yes, you’re reading this right. There’s a brand-new (sort of) JRPG that you’ve likely never played ripe for the taking right now! Surging Aura feels like it was meant to be Sega’s answer to Final Fantasy, but it has its own distinct personality and charm to where it feels like its own unique adventure.

We have the character and monster design of the late Mutsumi Inomata to thank for that. If you’re big on JRPGs, that name might sound familiar. She was the character designer for the Tales of series starting with Tales of Destiny. So, if you’ve been a fan of her work, this game is calling out to you specifically. It’s worth your time, I promise.

While some JRPGs disappear, others return from oblivion after years without new releases.

#4278. "You Don't Want To Interrupt The Player's Experience" - Here's Why Zelda's Switch 2 Remake Cut Some Mario References

Nintendo is known in recent times for dropping Star Fox (and even Pikmin) into the Super Mario universe, but with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, it decided to take a little more care.

In the castle courtyard, where Link meets with Zelda, you might have noticed how the character portraits for Mario and friends are not in the Switch 2 version of the game. If you are wondering about the thought process behind this, Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma has explained how the team didn't want to break the immersion.

Here's what he had to say during the same chat with Game Informer:

Eiji Aonuma: "Certainly, at the time, when we put those [portraits] there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, "Why is Yoshi there?” We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

If you recall, the 3DS game also had Skyward Sword art hidden in certain locations, and this is also gone from the Switch 2 remake. According to Aonuma, the same reasoning applies here - the team didn't want to "interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game".

Although these easter eggs are gone, certain references to the Mario series remain intact as they are part of the character designs:

"You will remember that there is one design element on Talon with Bowser on it, and that's part of the original design of the character. So we didn't change that. That stays as is."

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters.

There’s no reason they need to treat an all-time classic as a museum piece, because the original game will always be a masterpiece. Better to iterate upon it with fresh ideas and convenient tweaks than to declare any changes off-limits because of Nostalgia™.

The only major thing I would have done differently is to preserve the more poetic and succinct quality of the original English translation. I understand why they changed it for new audiences, but I still miss the original’s grand tone, and that’s one reason the 64 and 3DS versions will always have a place for me.

In general immersion is not something I have ever remotely cared about and I'd a lot rather just keep the random goofy references, but it's also not exactly a dealbreaker.

#4276. Mecha Domination codes (November 2026)

Every essential resource in the game including diamonds, boosts, food and water can be obtained through most of the Mecha Domination codes.

It’s common among mobile games these days to offer gift codes that you can redeem for free rewards. Often time-sensitive, these gift codes can give you a boost by providing valuable resources like premium currency. Mecha Domination's developer releases codes occasionally, and you'll definitely want to take advantage when they do. You can find a list of active Mecha Domination codes below. Active codes for Mecha Domination

How to redeem Mecha Domination codes? To redeem a code in Mecha Domination: Rampage, open the game and tap on your avatar in the top left corner of the screen. Then click on Settings and tap Redeem Code. Type the gift code into the text box shown and click the confirm button to receive your rewards immediately.

New Mecha Domination codes are released periodically, typically during special events and anniversaries. You can find new codes by checking out the game's official accounts on Instagram, Facebook, Reddit, Discord, and X (Twitter).

Looking for codes for other strategy games? Then you may want to go through our list of codes, which includes Top Troops codes, LDoE bunker alpha codes and many others.

About Mecha Domination Available for download via the App Store and Google Play, Mecha Domination: Rampage is a single-player casual mobile strategy game in which mechanised beasts have decimated the earth, displacing human civilisations. After centuries of wars and massacres, you rise up as a commander to save the remnants of humanity.

You’ll explore a vast world full of terrifying mechanised creatures and meet survivors who need your help. Build a shelter to protect your people and modify it to your heart's content using the remains of your colossal fallen foes. Train troops, capture and modify beasts, and form alliances as you journey across the wastes. As you progress, you'll build an army of beasts, including Scorchers, Spikerollers, and Sickleclaws.

#4275. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

#4273. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.
